question: Failure by the Xunta of Galicia to enlarge the Natura network along the boundaries of SAC ES11/0014 (Serra do Careón)

The autonomous government of Galicia (the Xunta) has breached the multiple EU warnings issued by the Commission since 2011 to enlarge the Natura Network protected area in Galicia, as well as an agreement of the Galician Parliament of June 2017 calling for this enlargement.

In the context of the open infringement procedure, the fact that the enlargement has not taken place is all the more serious given that the Xunta is exploiting this lack of protection to support projects that harm the environment and fail to comply with EU legislation.

In its responses to several of my questions, the Commission explained that the Galician Government’s contribution to the Natura Network was one of the lowest not only in Spain (27 %), but in the European Union as a whole, with 11.74 % of its surface area classed as protected.

I would like to raise concerns about the failure to enlarge the protected area in view of the threat posed by a cellulose plant project run by the company Greenfiber in an area bordering SAC ES11/0014 (Serra do Careón), which should have been enlarged several years ago. 1.
Does the Commission have confirmation of the request from the State and the Xunta to enlarge this area?
Will it urge the Galician Government and the Spanish Government to comply with the legal obligation to enlarge the Natura Network in Galicia?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.5.2024) Pursuant to the Habitats Directive1, Member States must contribute to the creation of Natura 2000 in proportion to the representation within their territory of the protected natural habitat types2 and the habitats of species3.

The Commission assesses the representation of each type of natural habitat or habitat of species in the context of biogeographic regions rather than on the basis of individual sites or administrative subdivisions. Consequently, the Commission cannot comment on the commitments made by the Spanish authorities at domestic level to enlarge a specific site.

In 2016, the Commission launched an investigation on the completion of the designation of Natura 2000 sites in Spain, after having detected several insufficiencies as a result of an update of its assessment of the Spanish national network of Sites of Community Importance.

The outcome of this investigation showed that Spain had failed to contribute to the creation of the Natura 2000 network in proportion to the representation within its territory of the relevant natural habitat types and habitats of the species. Accordingly, the Commission decided to send a letter of formal notice to Spain on 28 September 20234.
The Commission is currently assessing the observations submitted by Spain in reply to this letter in order to decide on the most appropriate action for this case.
1 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and

flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7–50. 2 Specified in Annex I to the Habitats Directive. 3 Specified in Annex II to the Habitats Directive. 4 In the framework of infringement procedure INFR(2023)2037. https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_23_4367
